decisions.statement: An addon folder with a tsconfig is built from the tsconfig held there.
An addon folder with no tsconfig is built from settings written into the build output.
The written settings name the module the addon page says the bundle starts from.
The written settings reach every module code file the addon folder has.
The written settings reach every declaration the addon folder has.
The written settings reach every declaration an addon this addon depends on holds.
The addons an addon depends on are the ones the game's own manifest names.
An addon depended on is found by the name that addon's own manifest states.
The addons an addon depends on are walked through to the end rather than a single level deep.
A dependency no addon in the checkout carries is left out of the compile.
The written settings reach every declaration a temper folder that is no addon holds.
A folder holding an addon page keeps its declarations to that addon.
The game's own names are described by the akasha folders of declarations.
The written settings say TypeScript emits nothing and the Lua is written anyway.
A reach spelled from the repository root down carries the file's own extension.
No setting here rewrites an extension.
An addon page naming no bundle entry answers that nothing can be built.
An addon page naming a bundle entry no module page carries refuses the call.
Where a bundle entry's code sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
A slug naming a page drops the page type spelled ahead of the slug.
Every module name in the bundle is worked out from the repository root down.
A settings file written here is named to the caller as soon as it is written.

definition: the transpiler settings a build reads for an addon whose folder has no tsconfig
